body: For what it's worth, this doesn't happen if the user specifically clicks inside `aio-search-box`, presumably because it stops propagation. If you set up a click listener on every child of `aio-shell` that does the same, the issue goes away, leading to the conclusion that `aio-shell` should be the culprit. How or why, I have no idea just yet.

A click on `aio-shell` closes the search box and calls `setSearch`, which in turn uses the native history API to `replaceState`, which triggers the behavior. Perhaps something is subscribed to the location change, that triggers this behavior.

@onlyflix While it's true that @gkalpak's solution still leaves room for this Chromium bug (that's supposedly fixed, by the way), it produces **_much less_** erroneous requests. In any case, Chrome loads these favicons from disk cache (according to the Network log), so I don't think there's much harm in it happening every once in a while.

I have to agree to that. The solution fixes most of the downloads, the rest is an issue on Chromiums site. 😉

But the bug actually isn't fixed, I did some more digging and found [this Chromium bug](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=895175), which is only 4 days old.
The fetching of all favicons happens because Chromium does not support the `sizes` attribute on link elements.
@onlyflix Good find! Would you care to open a PR?

<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->
On every click on the `aio-shell` `locationService.setSearch` gets called, which fetches all favicons because of [this Chromium bug](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=895175).

Issue Number: #26544 


## What is the new behavior?
`locationService.setSearch` is not getting called when the search is empty.

Favicons still get fetched on a click on an \<a\>-tag, which is a [known Chromium bug](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=895175), because Chromium doesn't support the `size` attribute on \<link\>-tags.
